mainTopic: The people of יריחו; reaping for fodder (קוצר לשחת), whether it divides a field for פאה, and whose view רבי מאיר follows
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא listing practices of the people of יריחו that the חכמים protested. The גמרא counts the items in that ברייתא and removes 'reaping' from its list, so it no longer clashes with our משנה. Next comes a new line from our משנה: one may reap young grain as animal fodder. The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת פאה listing what divides a field for פאה. In that משנה, רבי מאיר says reaping for fodder divides the field, and the חכמים say it divides only if the area was also plowed. The גמרא then tries to find whose view רבי מאיר follows. רבי שמעון is ruled out by a ברייתא about bugs and wind. רבי יהודה is ruled out because his rule covers only animal food. רב דימי says רבי מאיר follows his teacher רבי עקיבא, based on a משנה about cutting a field in patches, as limited by שמואל. The amud ends with רבין's report that challenges שמואל's limit, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The practices the חכמים protested
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. These are the practices of the people of יריחו that the חכמים protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would allow use of הקדש branches of carob and sycamore trees. They broke openings in their gardens and orchards so the poor could eat fallen fruit in drought years, on שבת and יום טוב. They gave פאה from vegetables. And the חכמים protested against them.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא about the people of יריחו. This part lists the three things the חכמים protested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא listed the things the חכמים did not protest, and reaping and piling grain before the עומר was on that list. 'Not protested' is weaker than our משנה's 'with the חכמים' approval'. That gap is the problem the גמרא deals with in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Branches of a tree
Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
Fruit that has fallen from the tree
The corner of a field left for the poor
They protested against them

phrases.english: They would permit consecrated branches
of carob and of sycamore trees,
and they would break openings in their gardens and their orchards
in order to feed fallen fruit to the poor
in years of drought
on Shabbatot and on Festivals,
and they would give pe'ah from vegetables,
and they protested against them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים protested these three practices of the people of יריחו.

steps.title: The count proves reaping does not belong on the list
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'six things', but its list adds up to seven. So the item 'reaping' is removed from the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, it says six? There are seven! Rather, remove 'reaping' from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא seemed to say reaping before the עומר was only not protested, while our משנה says it was done with the חכמים' approval. The גמרא answers by counting the items in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opened with 'six things'. Reaping and piling count as two separate acts, so the list really has seven. That shows reaping does not belong in the ברייתא, so the ברייתא says nothing about reaping and no longer contradicts our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning: turns a point back on the asker
Remove from here: take a word or item out of the text
Reaping, cutting the grain

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying reaping was forbidden. It removes 'reaping' from the ברייתא's list, so the ברייתא is silent about it and the משנה's 'with approval' stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's count of 'six' only works if reaping is removed, so our משנה's statement that reaping was done with the חכמים' approval is not contradicted.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, six?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא opened by saying the people of יריחו did 'six things'.

phrases.english: There are seven!
phrases.notes: Reaping and piling are counted as two separate items.

phrases.english: Rather, remove reaping from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the clash between the ברייתא just finished and our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא based on its own count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says reaping before the עומר was only 'not protested', which clashes with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Reaping is not part of the ברייתא's list, so there is no clash.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Reaping before the עומר was done with the חכמים' approval, as our משנה says.

steps.title: New topic: reaping crops for animal fodder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה: one may reap for fodder and feed it to an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may reap for fodder and feed it to an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a line from our משנה. This is a setup line for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה allows cutting young grain as animal food even before the עומר. The גמרא will now bring a related משנה about whether this kind of reaping affects the field in other areas of הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Reaping young grain to use as fodder
Green, unripe grain used as animal feed

phrases.english: One reaps for fodder and feeds it to an animal.
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from our משנה, which allows this even before the עומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יריחו discussion and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may reap young grain for fodder and feed it to an animal.

steps.title: What divides a field for פאה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מסכת פאה lists things that split one field into separate fields, each needing its own פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: These divide a field for פאה: a stream, a canal, a private road, a public road, a public path or private path that is used all year, summer and rainy season, a fallow field, a plowed field, and a different kind of seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת פאה. It lists things that cut a field into separate parts for the מצוה of פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one of these runs through a field, each part counts as its own field and needs its own פאה. A path only divides the field if it is permanent and used all year round. This list sets up the מחלוקת about reaping for fodder in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide or separate the field
A water channel or canal
A narrow path
Unplowed, fallow land
Plowed land
A different kind of crop

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פאה 2:1.

phrases.english: And these divide a field for pe'ah:
a stream, and a canal,
and a private road, and a public road,
and a public path, and a private path
that is permanent in the summer and in the rainy season,
and a fallow field, and a plowed field, and another kind of seed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה connected to the topic of reaping for fodder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These features split a field into separate fields, each needing its own פאה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and the חכמים on reaping for fodder
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that reaping for fodder divides a field for פאה. The חכמים say it divides only if the person also plowed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who reaps for fodder, that divides the field. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: it does not divide unless he plowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The same משנה ends with a מחלוקת about whether reaping part of a field for fodder splits the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the cut area alone separates the two parts of the field. The חכמים say cutting alone is not enough. Only once he plows that area does it become a 'plowed field' (ניר), which is already on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: He plowed
Unless

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: reaping for fodder divides the field for פאה. The חכמים: only if he also plowed it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת ties straight back to our משנה's case of קוצר לשחת and prepares the גמרא's next discussion.

phrases.english: And one who reaps for fodder divides the field,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir,
and the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַפְסִיק אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן חָרַשׁ.
phrases.english: It does not divide unless he plowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקוֹצֵר לְשַׁחַת מַפְסִיק, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the quoted משנה from פאה with a מחלוקת about reaping for fodder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: reaping for fodder divides the field. The חכמים: only if the area was also plowed.

steps.title: רבי מאיר follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר's ruling about פאה matches רבי שמעון's view that reaping for fodder is never real reaping, even after the grain reached a third.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר said his ruling following רבי שמעון's view. רבי שמעון says one may reap and feed animals even after the grain reached a third of its growth. So he must hold that any reaping for fodder is not counted as reaping.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the reason behind רבי מאיר's ruling from Step 5. He ties it to רבי שמעון's opinion in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows reaping for fodder even after the grain reached a third, which shows he does not count fodder-reaping as real reaping. רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר thinks the same way. That is why, for רבי מאיר, fodder-reaping is not the start of the field's harvest, so it splits the field for פאה even at that late stage.

keyTerms.meaning: following the view of
one third of its full growth, the point when grain counts as real produce
for fodder (cutting young grain to feed animals)
apparently / this shows that
reaping, harvesting

steps.whyThisMatters: This claim says רבי מאיר's ruling applies even after the grain reached a third. The objection that follows attacks exactly that point.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said it following the view of Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: "It" is רבי מאיר's ruling from Step 5, that reaping for fodder divides a field for פאה.

phrases.english: who says: one may reap and feed it to animals
even after it has reached a third of its growth.
Apparently he holds
that any reaping for fodder is not considered reaping.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's view in Step 5 by linking it to רבי שמעון in our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר holds like רבי שמעון: reaping for fodder, even after a third, is not real reaping, so it divides the field.

steps.title: Objection from bugs and wind damaging the field
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא brings a ברייתא: if bugs or wind destroyed a patch, all agree it divides the field only if it was plowed. "All" must include רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה was sitting and teaching this ruling. רב אחא בר הונא objected from a ברייתא: if grasshoppers ate a patch, or ants nibbled it, or the wind broke it down, all agree that if it was plowed it divides the field, and if not plowed it does not divide. Who is "all agree"? רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: An objection begins. The גמרא brings a ברייתא and points out that רבי מאיר agrees to it. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally רבי מאיר says fodder-reaping divides a field even without plowing. Here he agrees that a patch destroyed by bugs or wind divides only if plowed. This sets up a clash with רבי יוחנן's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: grasshopper
nibbled it away
everyone agrees, even the one who usually disagrees
plowed
divides (splits the field into separate fields for פאה)

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבָּה וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rabba was sitting and saying this teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Huna raised an objection to Rava:
If grasshoppers ate it,
or ants nibbled it away,
or the wind broke it down,
all agree that if he plowed there, it divides the field,
and if he did not plow, it does not divide.
"All agree": who is meant? Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן's explanation in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי מאיר follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר agrees that damage by bugs or wind divides a field only with plowing. The next step shows why this clashes with Step 6.

steps.title: Bugs should divide the field even more
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר's ruling were about grain before a third, there would be no problem. But if it is about grain after a third, then bug damage should divide the field all the more, and the ברייתא says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works fine if you say the משנה is talking about grain that had not reached a third, and the ברייתא (plowed: yes, not plowed: no) is talking about grain that had reached a third. But if you say the משנה is also about grain that reached a third, then think about it: there, where a person really reaped, רבי מאיר said it is not called reaping. Here, with bugs, shouldn't that be true all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא spells out his objection. He shows that רבי יוחנן's explanation leads to a contradiction in רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר's fodder ruling applied only before a third, it would not clash with the ברייתא, since that case is after a third. But רבי יוחנן said רבי מאיר follows רבי שמעון even after a third. Then a person cutting fodder is 'not reaping', and bugs eating should be 'not reaping' even more, so it should divide without plowing. Yet the ברייתא says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: it works fine if you say
but if you say (here is the problem)
a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה
all the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Here "not called reaping" is what makes a patch divide the field. So the 'all the more' argument says bug damage should divide without plowing, which is the opposite of what the ברייתא says.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's explanation makes רבי מאיר's fodder ruling apply after a third. That leads to a קל וחומר against the ברייתא about bugs and wind.

phrases.english: It works fine if you say
the משנה is where it had not reached a third,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פאה from Step 5, where רבי מאיר says reaping for fodder divides the field.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרַיְיתָא דְּחָרַשׁ – אִין, לֹא חָרַשׁ – לֹא,
phrases.english: and the ברייתא, which says plowed: yes, not plowed: no,
is where it had reached a third.
But if you say
the משנה is also where it had reached a third,
now, if there, where it is actual reaping,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָתָם אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: לֹא שְׁמָהּ קְצִירָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said there: it is not called reaping,
then here, is it not so all the more?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מַתְנִיתִין בְּשֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיאָה שְׁלִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא from Step 7 contradicts רבי יוחנן's explanation in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי מאיר's ruling applies even after a third, like רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if a person's fodder-reaping after a third is not called reaping, bugs eating after a third should be 'not reaping' even more and should divide without plowing. But the ברייתא, which רבי מאיר agrees to, says it needs plowing.

steps.title: A new answer: רבי מאיר follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רבי יוחנן's link to רבי שמעון. It says instead that רבי מאיר follows רבי יהודה, who makes a difference between grain before a third and grain after a third.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי מאיר said his rule following רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה says that cutting fodder is allowed only if the person started before the grain reached a third. If he started after it reached a third, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to explain רבי מאיר so that the problem from the bug-damage ברייתא goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, cutting grain before a third is not real reaping, but after a third it is. So רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה is about grain before a third, and that cutting divides the field. Grain after a third counts as the start of the real harvest, so it divides only with plowing, which fits the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: following the view of
When? (רבי יהודה's word for spelling out exactly when the rule applies)
a third: the stage when the grain has reached a third of its full growth
forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Meir said it following the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: When?
phrases.notes: He means: when may a person cut grain as animal food before the עומר? That's the case in the משנה about fodder.

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִתְחִיל עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁלִישׁ,
phrases.english: At a time that he started before it reached a third,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הִתְחִיל עַד שֶׁהֵבִיא שְׁלִישׁ – אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if he started after it reached a third, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יוחנן's explanation, which was knocked down in steps 7-8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change which תנא רבי מאיר follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר follows רבי שמעון, so even grain after a third is not real reaping
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר follows רבי יהודה: only grain before a third is not real reaping, so the ברייתא about grain after a third is no problem

steps.title: רבי יהודה only spoke about animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. רבי יהודה's rule was about cutting food for animals, and we have no proof he said it about food for people. If he had, there would be three opinions instead of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say you heard רבי יהודה say this about animal food. But did you hear him say it about food for people? If he had, there would be three different תנאים arguing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 9: רבי יהודה's rule may not reach as far as רבי מאיר's case needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's 'when?' only explains the first view in the משנה. It does not start a new argument. If he also allowed cutting for people before a third, he would be a separate third opinion, so his rule must stay limited to animal food.

keyTerms.meaning: for an animal
for a person
three תנאים: three separate opinions in one argument

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִבְהֵמָה,
phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yehuda say this for an animal,
for a person, did you hear him?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן, הָווּ לְהוּ תְּלָתָא תַּנָּאֵי.
phrases.english: For if so, there would be three Tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִבְהֵמָה, לְאָדָם מִי שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's distinction is only proven for animal food. Stretching it to food for people would make him a third, arguing opinion, which his 'when?' style does not allow.

steps.title: רב דימי: רבי מאיר follows his teacher רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי gives a different source. רבי מאיר follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that cutting unripe grain is not real reaping even when it is for people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רב דימי came, he said: רבי מאיר said his rule following his teacher רבי עקיבא. Even when the cutting is for people, it does not count as reaping.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי יהודה did not work, the גמרא brings רב דימי's answer, which uses a תנא whose view covers food for people too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's view fixes the gap from step 10, because it is not limited to animal food. The proof for this view comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: when he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching)
his teacher
reaping, harvesting that counts as the real harvest

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rather, when Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אָמַר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said it following the view of Rabbi Akiva, his teacher,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְאָדָם נָמֵי לָא הָוְיָא קְצִירָה.
phrases.english: even for a person, too, it is not reaping.

steps.title: The משנה about cutting a field in spots
steps.stepSummary: Proof for רבי עקיבא's view. When a person cuts a field in patches and leaves moist stalks between them, רבי עקיבא says each patch needs its own פאה. The חכמים say one פאה covers the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if someone cuts a field in spots and leaves moist stalks in it, רבי עקיבא says each patch needs its own פאה. The חכמים say he gives פאה from one patch for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה in פאה to show where רבי עקיבא's view comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the cut patches count as separate fields. So cutting grain that was still moist did not count as one continuous harvest. The חכמים treat the whole field as one.

steps.title: שמואל: רבי עקיבא means only unripe grain
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits רבי עקיבא's rule. Separate פאה is needed only when the grain was cut unripe for roasting. When it was cut ripe for storage, the whole field is one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי עקיבא required separate פאה only when a person cut the field in spots for roasted grain. When he cut it in spots for the storehouse, he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains exactly when רבי עקיבא's rule applies, and this completes רב דימי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting unripe grain for roasting, even as food for people, is not real reaping, so it divides the field. Cutting ripe grain for storage is real reaping and does not divide it. That fits רבי מאיר: the משנה is about unripe grain, while the ברייתא is about fully grown grain.

keyTerms.meaning: roasted grain, made from unripe kernels

steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי's answer: רבי מאיר follows רבי עקיבא. With שמואל's limit, cutting unripe grain is not real reaping, even for people, so it divides a field for פאה. Cutting fully grown grain is real reaping and divides only with plowing. The next step challenges this.

steps.title: רבין reports that רבי עקיבא requires separate פאה even for grain cut for storage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's limit. רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that רבי עקיבא requires separate פאה for each patch even when ripe grain is cut for storage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי עקיבא required separate פאה for each patch even when someone cut patches of grain to put in the storehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions שמואל's limit on רבי עקיבא's rule. It brings a report that says רבי עקיבא's rule applies even to ripe grain cut for storage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said רבי עקיבא requires separate פאה only for unripe grain cut for roasting. רבין's report says רבי עקיבא requires it even for ripe grain cut for storage. If that is right, then for רבי עקיבא even cutting ripe grain does not count as starting to reap the whole field. That would no longer match רבי מאיר, who holds that cutting grain after it is a third grown does count as reaping.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so?" The גמרא is doubting a statement it just heard.
"When he came." Used when a sage brings a teaching from ארץ ישראל to בבל.
Obligates. Here: requires separate פאה for each patch.
Cutting in patches, leaving uncut stalks between them.
Storehouse. Grain is put there when it is ripe and cut for keeping.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is attacking רבי עקיבא's basic rule from step 12. Everyone agrees he requires separate פאה for each patch. The only question is how far the rule goes: just unripe grain (שמואל), or also ripe grain cut for storage (רבין).
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof that רבי מאיר follows רבי עקיבא (step 11) depends on שמואל's limit. If רבין is right, that link is in danger.

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that רבי עקיבא requires separate פאה only for grain cut unripe for roasting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבין, quoting רבי יוחנן, says רבי עקיבא requires separate פאה even for ripe grain cut for storage. That directly contradicts שמואל's limit. It also threatens the claim that רבי מאיר follows רבי עקיבא.
